items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1960-12-20
items.q: Now Teo was the man who used to sip his reeds. That's why today I used to sip the reeds.

ctx.x: Who was your favorite clarinetist that you liked more than the others? Any one person or a couple of them? Yeah, Louie.

You liked Louie? I liked Louie the best. Somehow or another, I don't know. Any way he was playing, I dragged him, I know that I dragged on. That's Big Eye Louie. Big Eye Louie. Yeah. I dragged him, and then after that I liked to heal. Now Teo was the man who used to sip his reeds. That's why today I used to sip the reeds. He used to step?

items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1960-07-29
items.q: Oh, that was a good man. He was on the dots and he was jazz.

ctx.x: Did he ever play any jazz?

Well, those men wasn't much on jazz. Louis was a man on jazz. We got Louis. They said Piku, Manana, and all them, you know, them guys that was on the dots. Brockie and all that folks. They said Piku, Manana, and all them. How about Teal? Teal? Oh, that was a good man. He was on the dots and he was jazz. He was on the dots and he was on jazz. How about Teal?
How about Teal? Did he ever play any jazz, Nicholas?
